cards.front: Which organelle makes most of a cell's ATP?
Why do plant cells keep their shape when water is plentiful?
cards.back: Water pressure inside the cell pushes the membrane against the rigid wall.

cards.front: What is the gas exchanged through stomata during the day?
cards.back: Carbon dioxide enters; oxygen and water vapour leave.

cards.front: A leaf is kept in the dark for two days. Predict what happens to its starch store and say why.
cards.back: It falls. Without light the plant cannot make new sugar, so stored starch is used up.

cards.front: Osmosis versus diffusion: what extra condition defines osmosis?
cards.back: Only water moves, across a partially permeable membrane.

cards.front: Which stage of respiration needs oxygen?
cards.back: The electron transport chain, at the end.

cards.front: Red blood cells have no nucleus. What does that allow?
cards.back: More room to carry haemoglobin, so more oxygen per cell.

cards.front: Salt is added to a potato slice in water. Predict the slice's mass change.
cards.back: It loses mass, because water leaves the cells by osmosis.
